message.abstract: <jats:p>Reliable multistep prediction of floating wind‐farm wakes is constrained by recurrent error growth, scarce target‐condition data, and ambiguity between commanded nacelle yaw and passive platform yaw. To address these issues, a hierarchical model is constructed in this study: starting from a data‐driven ConvLSTM baseline, it introduces a PI‐ConvLSTM with weak penalties on horizontal divergence, reduced momentum transport, and temporal increments, and finally upgrades to a Meta‐PI‐ConvLSTM for few‐shot adaptation. Nacelle yaw and platform yaw are encoded separately, while wake fields and farm power are predicted jointly. Using fixed‐bottom FAST.Farm/OpenFAST trajectories for source‐task learning and a short floating sequence for adaptation, the framework reduces source‐field MAE by 74.7%, decreases global and wake‐region target MAE by 31.6% and 35.4%, respectively, lowers wake‐center MAE from 6.73 m to 4.93 m, and cuts power MAE from 1.314 MW to 0.628 MW in the matched numerical case.</jats:p>
title: Platform-Yaw-Aware Physics-Informed,Meta-Learning for Floating Wind Farm Wake and Power Prediction
